questions.stem: Which of the following is a typical property of metals?

options.text: They are poor conductors of electricity
They are malleable and can be hammered into sheets
They usually have low melting points

questions.explanation: Metals are typically malleable, meaning they can be hammered or pressed into sheets without breaking. This is because layers of metal ions can slide over each other while remaining held together by delocalised electrons.

questions.stem: Why are metals good conductors of electricity?

options.text: Because they have high melting points
Because they have delocalised electrons that are free to move and carry charge

questions.explanation: In metallic bonding, outer electrons become delocalised (free to move throughout the metal structure). These free-moving electrons can carry electrical charge through the metal, making metals good conductors of electricity.
